summary: supercolor-tui ships a Windows dropper that disables Defender and executes a Discord-CDN-hosted EXE on first use
details: The package presents itself as a terminal color library, but on Windows the first invocation of any Color method (print/paint/__call__) calls an internal _run_payload routine that (1) invokes PowerShell with Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath and -ExclusionProcess to add Microsoft Defender exclusions for %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime and the dropped binary, (2) downloads an opaque executable from https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1560347732839891076/1562446203021566032/bedwars.exe via urllib.request.urlopen with no integrity check, (3) writes the bytes to %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime\bedwars.exe, and (4) launches it detached via subprocess.Popen with DETACHED_PROCESS. The Discord CDN URL is an anonymous, mutable, author-controlled host unrelated to any legitimate color-library publisher, and the Defender-exclusion step is explicit anti-forensics paired with the drop. The library's advertised terminal-color purpose provides no justification for fetching and executing a Windows binary or modifying Defender policy.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
